title: Aranygaluska (Hungarian golden dumpling pull-apart cake with walnuts)
steps: Mix the yeast with a spoon of sugar and the warm milk and leave it to foam for 10 minutes.
Add the flour, sugar, 2 egg yolks, salt and 20 g of the melted butter and knead into a soft dough. Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Roll the dough out to 1.5 cm thick and cut it into small squares or walnut-sized pieces. Roll them into balls.
Mix the walnuts and the coating sugar. Dip each ball in melted butter and roll it in the walnut mixture.
Pile the balls loosely in a buttered bundt or loaf tin, let rise for 20 minutes, then bake at 180 C for about 30 to 35 minutes until golden.
For the custard, whisk the milk, yolks, sugar, vanilla and cornflour in a saucepan and heat gently, stirring, until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Turn the cake out onto a plate and serve warm with the custard.

title: Brassói aprópecsenye (Hungarian Brasov-style pork with garlic and roasted potatoes)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or loin, cut into 3 cm chunks
potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
pickled cucumbers or beetroot, to serve

steps: Season the pork with salt and pepper. Heat half the lard in a large pan and fry the meat over high heat until browned on all sides.
Add the onion and fry for 2 minutes, then add 100 ml of water, cover and cook gently for about 25 minutes until the pork is tender.
Meanwhile, fry the potato cubes in the remaining lard in a second large pan, turning often, for about 15 to 20 minutes until crisp and golden. Salt them.
Stir the crushed garlic and marjoram into the pork for the last 3 minutes.
Combine the potatoes with the meat and toss together briefly over the heat.
Serve with pickled cucumbers or beetroot.

title: Dobos torta (Hungarian six-layer sponge cake with chocolate cream and caramel top)

ingredients.name: caster sugar, for the caramel top
lemon juice or neutral oil, to grease the knife

steps: Whisk the 6 eggs with the sugar and salt in a bowl over simmering water until warm, then whisk off the heat until pale, thick and tripled in volume. Fold in the sifted flour gently.

Draw six 20 cm circles on baking paper. Spread a thin layer of batter on each and bake one or two at a time at 200 C for 5 to 7 minutes until pale gold. Keep the best-looking layer for the top and trim the others to the same size.
For the cream, whisk the 3 eggs with the icing sugar over simmering water until thick and about 70 C, then whisk off the heat until cool.
Beat the soft butter into the cooled egg mixture a spoonful at a time and fold in the melted chocolate.
Layer five sponge circles with the chocolate cream, and spread the remaining cream around the sides.

Melt the caster sugar in a dry pan, without stirring, until it becomes an amber caramel. Pour it at once on the reserved layer, spread it thin and cut it into 12 wedges with an oiled knife before it sets.
Arrange the wedges on top of the cake and chill for several hours before serving.

title: Esterházy torta (Hungarian walnut meringue layer cake with cognac cream)
steps: Whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks, gradually adding the sugar, until the meringue is glossy. Fold in the ground nuts and flour gently.
Draw four 20 cm circles on baking paper, spread the mixture in thin even layers and bake at 160 C for about 25 minutes until pale gold. Cool completely.
For the cream, whisk the egg yolks with the sugar and milk over low heat, stirring, until thick, then cool.
Beat the butter until fluffy, add the cooled custard a spoonful at a time and flavour with the cognac.
Sandwich the meringue layers with the cream and cover the top and sides with a thin coat, saving some cream for decoration.
Brush the top with warmed apricot jam, then spread it with icing sugar mixed with a few spoons of warm water into a smooth glaze.
Pipe thin lines of melted chocolate across the glaze, drag a toothpick through them in alternating directions to make the feathered pattern, and chill before slicing.

title: Fánk (Hungarian yeast doughnuts with apricot jam)

ingredients.name: oil or lard for deep frying

steps: Stir the yeast and a pinch of the sugar into the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix in the flour, remaining sugar, egg yolks, butter, rum and salt and knead for 10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Roll the dough out on a floured board to about 2 cm thick and cut out 6 cm rounds with a cutter. Place them on a floured cloth and let them rise for 20 to 30 minutes, covered.
Heat the oil to 170 C in a wide deep pan. Fry the doughnuts, a few at a time, with the lid on for 2 minutes, then turn and fry uncovered for another 2 minutes, so a pale ring forms around the middle.
Drain on paper towels, dust with icing sugar and serve with apricot jam.

title: Flódni (Hungarian four-layer pastry with poppy seed, walnut, apple and plum jam)

ingredients.name: tart apples, peeled and coarsely grated

steps: Rub the butter into the flour and icing sugar, then mix in the yolks and sour cream and knead briefly. Divide the dough into 5 pieces, wrap and chill for an hour.
For the poppy layer, heat the poppy seeds with 100 g sugar and the milk until thick, then cool.
Mix the walnuts with 80 g sugar and a splash of milk for the walnut layer.
Cook the apples with 60 g sugar and the cinnamon for 10 minutes to evaporate the juice, then cool.
Roll out each piece of dough to the size of a 20 by 30 cm tin. Line the tin with the first sheet and spread with the poppy filling.
Add a second sheet, then the walnut layer, a third sheet, the apple layer, a fourth sheet and the plum jam, and top with the fifth sheet. Prick the top with a fork.
Bake at 180 C for about 40 minutes until golden, cool completely and dust with icing sugar before cutting into squares.

title: Főzelék (Hungarian thick vegetable stew, pea version)

ingredients.name: fried eggs or meatballs, to serve (optional)

steps: Simmer the peas in the water with a little salt and the sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until tender.
In a separate pan, heat the oil, stir in the flour and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it is golden, making a light roux.
Take the roux off the heat, stir in the paprika and garlic and pour in a ladleful of the pea cooking liquid, stirring until smooth.
Pour the roux mixture back into the peas and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until the stew is as thick as a loose porridge.
Season with salt and a little vinegar and stir in the parsley.
Serve hot, usually with a fried egg or meatballs on top.

title: Gundel palacsinta (Hungarian walnut-filled crêpes with chocolate sauce)

ingredients.name: oil, plus oil for the pan

steps: Soak the raisins in the rum for 30 minutes.
Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, sugar, oil and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter, rest it for 20 minutes, then cook 8 thin crêpes in a lightly oiled pan.
Warm the filling milk with the sugar, stir in the walnuts, zest and the raisins with their rum, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until you get a thick spreadable paste. Let it cool slightly.
Spread each crêpe with the filling, roll it up or fold it into quarters and arrange the pancakes in a shallow dish.
Heat the cream to just under a simmer, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir until glossy and smooth.
Warm the pancakes briefly in the oven if you like, then pour the hot chocolate sauce over them and serve.

title: Halászlé (Hungarian paprika fisherman's soup with carp)

ingredients.name: carp, whole or in steaks (with the head and bones for stock; or use a mix of river fish)
hot paprika, or 1 fresh hot chilli
thin soup pasta or egg noodles (optional)

steps: Clean and scale the fish, cut it into thick steaks and salt the pieces. Keep the head, tail and bones separate for the stock.
Put the onions in a pot with the fish heads, tails and bones, add the water and a little salt, and boil for 20 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the soft onions through with a spoon so they thicken the broth, and discard the bones.
Return the broth to the pot, stir in the sweet and hot paprika, then add the green pepper and tomato and simmer for 10 minutes.
Slide in the fish steaks, adding only enough water to cover if needed, and simmer gently for 10 to 12 minutes without stirring, shaking the pot now and then so the pieces stay whole.
If using pasta, cook it separately and add to bowls. Serve the soup very hot with bread.

title: Hortobágyi palacsinta (Hungarian crêpes filled with paprika meat stew)

ingredients.name: oil, plus oil for the pan
veal or beef stewing meat, finely diced

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, oil and a pinch of salt into a smooth thin batter and rest it for 20 minutes.
Cook thin crêpes in a lightly oiled pan, about 8 of them, and stack them to keep warm.
For the filling, soften the onion in oil, take off the heat and stir in the paprika, then add the meat, tomato, pepper and salt.
Add the water and simmer, covered, for about 1 hour until the meat is very tender and the liquid has reduced to a thick sauce. Shred the meat finely with two forks.
Fill each crêpe with a spoonful of the filling and fold into a parcel. Set them side by side in an ovenproof dish.
Whisk the flour into half the sour cream, stir in the remaining liquid from the stew pan, bring to a simmer for a couple of minutes, then pour it over the crêpes.
Heat in a 180 C oven for 10 minutes and serve with the remaining sour cream.

title: Kürtőskalács (Hungarian chimney cake)

ingredients.name: ground walnuts and 1 tsp cinnamon (for coating, optional)

steps: Mix the yeast and a spoon of sugar into the warm milk and leave to foam for 10 minutes.
Add the flour, remaining 60 g sugar, yolks, melted butter and salt, knead for 10 minutes into a smooth dough, then cover and rise for 1 hour.
Wrap two wooden rolling pins or cardboard tubes tightly in foil and grease them well with butter.
Roll the dough out to about 5 mm thick and cut it into a long strip about 2 cm wide. Wind the strip tightly around each tube in a spiral, slightly overlapping the edges, and press so the strips join.
Brush with melted butter, roll in the sugar (mixed with the nuts and cinnamon if using) and set the tubes across a baking tin so they hang clear of the tray.
Bake at 200 C for 20 to 25 minutes, turning and brushing with butter every 5 minutes, until deeply golden and caramelised.
Slide the cakes off the tubes while still warm and serve hot.

title: Lecsó (Hungarian pepper and tomato stew)

ingredients.name: yellow or green Hungarian wax peppers (or sweet pointed peppers), seeded and sliced into rings

steps: Heat the lard in a wide pan and cook the onion over medium-low heat for about 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Remove the pan from the heat, stir in the paprika, then return to the heat and immediately add the peppers.
Cook the peppers for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they start to soften.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and salt. If using sausage, add the slices now.
Cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until the vegetables are very soft and the juices have thickened.
For a fuller dish, beat the eggs lightly and stir them in for the last few minutes, or serve the lecsó plain with bread or rice.

title: Meggyleves (chilled Hungarian sour cherry soup)

ingredients.name: sour cherries, pitted (fresh, frozen or jarred and drained)

steps: Bring the water to a boil with the cinnamon, cloves, lemon zest, salt and sugar.
Add the cherries and simmer gently for about 10 minutes until they are soft.
In a bowl, whisk the flour into the sour cream until smooth, then whisk in a ladleful of the hot cherry liquid.
Pour this mixture slowly into the soup, stirring, and simmer for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Remove the cinnamon, cloves and zest. Taste and add sugar or a squeeze of lemon if needed.
Cool to room temperature, then chill for at least 3 hours. Serve cold.

title: Palóc soup (Hungarian lamb and green bean soup with sour cream and dill)

ingredients.name: green beans, cut in 3 cm pieces

steps: Fry the onion in the lard until golden, take it off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the lamb and salt and brown the meat lightly, then pour in the water and add the bay leaf.
Simmer, covered, for about 1 hour until the meat is almost tender.
Add the green beans and potatoes and simmer for a further 20 minutes until tender.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream, stir in a ladleful of hot soup, then pour it all back into the pot with the vinegar and simmer for 5 minutes without boiling hard.
Season, stir in the dill and serve hot.

title: Pörkölt (Hungarian paprika meat stew)

ingredients.name: beef chuck or shin (pork shoulder also works), cut into 3 cm cubes
nokedli (small dumplings), egg noodles or boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Soften the onions in the lard over medium-low heat for about 10 minutes until golden and soft, stirring so they do not catch.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika quickly, since it turns bitter if scorched.
Add the meat, garlic, caraway, bay leaf and salt and return to a medium heat, stirring until the meat has turned pale on the outside.
Cover and cook gently in the meat's own juices for 20 minutes, adding a splash of water only if the pan gets dry.
Add the pepper and tomatoes, and enough water to just barely cover the meat, then simmer, partly covered, for 1.5 to 2 hours until tender and the sauce is thick and rich.
Season to taste and serve hot with dumplings, noodles or potatoes and a pickled cucumber.

title: Rigó Jancsi (Hungarian chocolate sponge squares with chocolate cream)
steps: Beat the egg yolks with half the sugar until pale. In a clean bowl, whisk the whites with the remaining sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the yolks, then fold in the sifted flour and cocoa. Spread the batter in a lined 20 by 30 cm tin and bake at 180 C for 12 to 15 minutes. Cool.
For the filling, heat 100 ml of the cream, pour it over 200 g chopped chocolate and stir until smooth, then cool and chill until thick.
Whip the remaining 200 ml cream to soft peaks and fold it into the cooled chocolate mixture.
Cut the sponge into two equal rectangles, brush one with warmed jam and spread with the chocolate cream, then top with the second sponge.
Chill for 2 hours. Melt the glaze chocolate with the cream, spread it thinly over the top and cut into squares once set.

title: Székelykáposzta (Hungarian pork and sauerkraut stew with sour cream)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
sauerkraut, rinsed briefly if very sour and drained

steps: Soften the onion in the lard for about 8 minutes, then take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the pork, garlic, caraway, salt, pepper and a splash of water and cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the meat turns pale.
Add the sauerkraut and bay leaf with the remaining water. Cover and simmer for about 1 hour until the pork is tender.
Whisk the flour into the sour cream until smooth and stir a ladleful of hot liquid into it.
Pour the mixture into the pot and simmer for 5 more minutes without boiling hard, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve hot with a spoonful of extra sour cream and rye bread.

title: Tarhonya (Hungarian toasted egg barley side dish)

ingredients.name: tarhonya (egg barley), or substitute orzo or other small dried egg pasta

steps: Heat the lard in a wide pot over medium heat and add the tarhonya.
Stir constantly for 5 to 8 minutes until the pasta is golden brown and smells nutty.
Add the onion and cook for 2 minutes until softened, then stir in the paprika for a few seconds.
Pour in the hot water or stock all at once, season with salt and stir.
Cover and simmer on very low heat for 12 to 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed and the pasta is tender but separate.
Fluff with a fork and serve with stews such as pörkölt.

title: Túrós csusza (Hungarian noodles with curd cheese, bacon and sour cream)

ingredients.name: wide flat egg noodles or pasta squares
dry cottage cheese or curd cheese (túró), crumbled
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Boil the noodles in plenty of salted water until just tender, then drain well.
Fry the bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until the fat has melted out and the pieces are crisp and golden.
Add the drained noodles to the pan with the bacon and fat and toss for a minute.
Divide the noodles between plates and top each with a handful of crumbled curd cheese.
Add a generous spoonful of sour cream to each serving and season with pepper and a pinch of salt.
Sprinkle the crispy bacon over the top and serve immediately.
